title: contest.yaml, format_version 1
description: Declarative contest for `judgectl contest apply`. Times without an offset are in JUDGE_TIMEZONE. The state (draft/published/archived) and the invite code are not part of the file. Rules the schema cannot express (end after start, a freeze inside the window and not with a hidden leaderboard, a positive personal duration) are checked by the importer. See docs/CONTESTS.md.

ends_at.description: Absent or null: no end (a practice archive). Allowed with personal timing too: a timed practice.

freeze_at.description: Leaderboard freeze; needs ends_at and a leaderboard that is not hidden; not with personal timing.

mode.description: open: any student, with a button; code: with the invite code; groups: students now in one of `groups`, without a code; code_or_groups: either.

groups.description: Names of the groups (classes) the contest is addressed to; only with groups / code_or_groups, and then at least one. A group dropped from the list is detached.

access.description: Who may enter. Absent: mode code.

languages.description: Absent: every language enabled in the system.

time.description: ISO 8601; without Z or an offset it is local time of JUDGE_TIMEZONE.

version.description: Pinned version (must be ready). Absent: keep the current pin; when the problem is added, the latest ready version.

points.description: Overrides the total of the problem; group points are scaled proportionally.

available_from.description: Before it (inclusive from) the problem does not exist for students.

due_at.description: Deadline, inclusive: a submission received at due_at is on time. Extensions are given with `judgectl extension`, not here.

submit.description: no: refused; late: accepted and marked late; yes: accepted as usual.

after_due.description: What happens after the effective due moment; upsolving after the contest is not touched.

note_md.description: The teacher's note on this problem in this contest (Markdown), shown to students with access.
